findings:
STORAGE & SERIALIZATION
- The list of plans lives on the save-game root: `GameInstance.hrManagerPlans` — `public List<HrManagerPlan> hrManagerPlans = new List<HrManagerPlan>();` (GameInstance.cs:222). Reached everywhere as `SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans` (`SaveGameManager.Current` is the live `GameInstance`, SaveGameManager.cs:127).
- `GameInstance` is `[Serializable]`. `HrManagerPlan` is a plain class (HrManagerPlan.cs:10) with a `public readonly string id = UuidHelper.GenerateBase64Uuid();` plus public fields: `assignedEmployeeId` (string), `headquartersAddress` (Address), `assignedEmployees` (List<string> of EmployeeInstance ids), `replaceAbsentEmployees` (bool, default true), `trainingTarget` (int, default 50), `healthInsurancePlan` (HealthInsurancePlan, nullable). `_hrManagerInstance` is a private non-serialized cache, lazily rebuilt by `GetHrManagerInstance()`.
- Serialization (SaveGameSerializationHelper.cs): primary path is Odin `SerializationUtility.SerializeValue(instance, stream, DataFormat.Binary, ctx)` with `Player.SaveSystem.SaveGameSerializationPolicy` (Unity policy, `AllowNonSerializableTypes = true`, and it SKIPS any member marked `[Obsolete]`). Alternate/legacy path is Newtonsoft `JsonConvert.SerializeObject(instance, Formatting.None, settings)` with `TypeNameHandling.Auto` + `ReferenceLoopHandling.Ignore` (so subclasses get `$type`). Both serialize `hrManagerPlans` by walking the public field.
- The HR-manager EMPLOYEE is NOT stored in the plan; it is a normal entry in `GameInstance.EmployeeInstances` whose concrete type is the `HRManager` subclass — polymorphism preserved by Odin type metadata / Newtonsoft `$type`. The plan only keeps the string `assignedEmployeeId`.
- Health-insurance negotiation offers are stored separately: `GameInstance.healthInsurancePlanOffers` : `List<HealthInsurancePlanOffer>`, each carrying `hrManagerPlanId`.
- Plan ORDER in the list is meaningful: `HrManagersPlanList.UpdatePlanOrder` reorders `SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans` directly and calls `SaveGameManager.MarkChange()`; `HeadhuntersAutomaticReplacementTab` numbers plans by their index within a HQ.
- Compatibility fixes that touch it: `CompatibilityFixesEA06.UpdateHeadquartersPlansToNewSystem` (migrated old single-manager-per-HQ into the plan list), `CompatibilityFixesEA04.FixHRManagerNotHavingCorrectClass` (re-instantiates any hrmanager-skilled EmployeeInstance as `HRManager`), `CompatibilityFixesEA010.RemoveInvalidPlans` (drops plans whose HQ is no longer player-rented; nulls dangling `EmployeeInstance.assignedHrManagerPlanId`).

PLAN CREATION
- Created purely in UI by `HrManagersPlanList.AddPlan()` (the "+" button entry at the bottom of the HRManagers tab list): `new HrManagerPlan { headquartersAddress = InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.business.address }` → `SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans.Add(hrManagerPlan)` → `SetUpPlanEntry` → `SelectPlan` → `SaveGameManager.MarkChange()`.
- The ONLY field set at creation is `headquartersAddress`. `id` auto-generates. `assignedEmployeeId` is null → the detail panel shows `NoManagerAssignedPopUp`. There is no money cost and no skill/level gate to create a plan; a HQ can hold any number of plans.

THE HR-MANAGER EMPLOYEE LINK (assignedEmployeeId)
- It is a completely ordinary hired employee that happens to carry skill `ba:skill_hrmanager`; its runtime class is `Entities.HRManager : EmployeeInstance` ([Serializable]).
- Sourcing/hiring is the standard employee pipeline, no special path:
  * `RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate(skillName, skillValue, businessAddress, demands)` switches on skill: `"ba:skill_hrmanager" => new HRManager()` (RecruitmentHelper.cs:46). It adds the candidate to `SaveGameManager.Current.CandidateEmployeeInstances`, fires `ba:gameevent_candidatereceived`, bumps the MyEmployees app badge.
  * Candidates are produced by `RecruitmentCampaign.CheckForCandidates()` (player starts a paid campaign at a recruitment agency, picking `skillRequirement.skillName` + full/part-time) or by a Headhunter plan recruiting `ba:skill_hrmanager` (`HeadhunterPlan`, line ~178).
  * Player hires from MyEmployees > Candidates via `EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate(candidate)` (EmployeeHelper.cs:514): removes from candidates, finishes salary negotiation, adds to `SaveGameManager.Current.EmployeeInstances`, sets `dayHired`, adds an `EmployeeUnassigned/EmployeeIdle` todo, fires `ba:gameevent_employeehired`. After that it is a normal "My Employees" row (target 3 satisfied for the vanilla role).
- To be attachable to a plan the employee must additionally: be assigned to that HQ address (`assignedAddress == plan.headquartersAddress`) AND be on a WorkShift there (see SCHEDULING below).
- Plan API: `HrManagerPlan.AssignEmployee(string employeeId)` sets `assignedEmployeeId` and nulls the `_hrManagerInstance` cache; `UnAssignEmployee()` nulls both. `HrManagerInstance` => `EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById(assignedEmployeeId)` (lazy/cached). `HrManagerSkillValue => HrManagerInstance?.GetSkillValue("ba:skill_hrmanager") ?? 0f`.
- One manager per plan and one plan per manager: `HrManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForHrManager(id)` = `hrManagerPlans.FirstOrDefault(x => x.assignedEmployeeId == id)`; the UI candidate filter also enforces `!hrManagerPlans.Exists(y => y.id != plan.id && y.assignedEmployeeId == x.id)`.
- Capacity is a function of skill: `HrManagerPlan.MaxEmployees => HrManagerSkillValue.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees()`, and `HrManagerHelper.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees(this float skill) => 10 + Mathf.FloorToInt(skill / 5f / 5f) * 10` (HrManagerHelper.cs:40) → 10 (skill 0–24), 20 (25–49), 30 (50–74), 40 (75–99), 50 (100).

ASSIGNING THE HR MANAGER TO A PLAN (UI)
- `HrManagersPlanList.UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan` builds the per-entry "ManagerDropdown". The candidate pool: `SaveGameManager.Current.EmployeeInstances.FindAll(x => x.assignedAddress == <HQ address> && x.HasSkill("ba:skill_hrmanager") && !hrManagerPlans.Exists(y => y.id != plan.id && y.assignedEmployeeId == x.id) && x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift())` (HrManagersPlanList.cs:170).
- Selecting a name → `OnChangedHrManager` (validates new manager's MaxEmployees vs current `assignedEmployees.Count` and health-insurance min-skill, trimming the list after a `HudConfirm` if the new manager is weaker) → `ChangeHrManager` → `plan.AssignEmployee(newHrManager?.id)`.
- A plan with no manager shows `NoManagerAssignedPopUp` (top-level class NoManagerAssignedPopUp.cs) which has its own `employeeDropdown` wired to the same `OnChangedHrManager` path, plus the plan `Delete` button (`HrManagerHelper.DeletePlan(id)`).

SUPERVISED ENTITIES (assignedEmployees) — WHAT THE MANAGER ACTS ON
- `HrManagerPlan.assignedEmployees` : `List<string>` of `EmployeeInstance.id`. For the HR role these are the employees the manager TRAINS (there is no store concept in the vanilla HR plan). Reverse pointer: `EmployeeInstance.assignedHrManagerPlanId` (string, EmployeeInstance.cs:73).
- UI: the plan detail panel `HrManagerPlanUI`. `OpenAssignEmployeesList()` loads `assignableEmployeesScrollerController` (an `EmployeesScrollerController : BaTable<EmployeeCellView, HrManagerEmployeeModel>`). Each row is an `EmployeeCellView` with an `assignToggle`.
- Add/remove call: `HrManagerPlanUI.SetEmployeeAssigned(string employeeId, bool assigned, bool refreshData = true)` (HrManagerPlanUI.cs:256):
  * assign → `_currentPlan.assignedEmployees.Add(employeeId)` and `EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById(employeeId).assignedHrManagerPlanId = _currentPlan.id`.
  * unassign → `assignedEmployees.Remove(employeeId)` and `assignedHrManagerPlanId = null`.
  * then `onAssignedEmployeesChanged(NumberOfAssignedEmployees, MaxEmployees)` updates the "N/Max" label.
- Bulk helpers: `HrManagerPlanUI.Fill()` (assigns unassigned employees up to `MaxEmployees - NumberOfAssignedEmployees`), `ClearAssignedEmployees()`.
- Cap: `CanAssignEmployee() => _currentPlan.NumberOfAssignedEmployees < _currentPlan.MaxEmployees`; over-cap toggle shows `Notifications.Show(NotificationType.Error, "bizman_hrmanager_max_employees_reached", …)` and reverts.
- Candidate pool for assignment (`EmployeesScrollerController.Load`, includeUnassignedEmployees): `EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeInstances()` where `string.IsNullOrEmpty(instance.assignedHrManagerPlanId) && instance.id != managerId`. NOTE: NOT filtered by business/address — one HR manager can train employees across every business the player owns.
- Cleanup: `HrManagerPlan.Delete()` sets `assignedHrManagerPlanId = null` on every `EmployeeInstances` member, marks any matching `healthInsurancePlanOffers` finished, then `hrManagerPlans.RemoveAll(x => x.id == id)`. `EmployeeInstance.OnRemove` (EmployeeHelper-side, EmployeeInstance.cs:844) also does `HrManagerHelper.GetPlanFromId(assignedHrManagerPlanId)?.assignedEmployees.Remove(id)`. `TrainEmployees()` itself prunes null entries from `assignedEmployees` each run.

WHAT DRIVES THE PLAN EACH DAY
- Chain: `GameManager.NewDay()` → `EmployeeHelper.PayDailyWages()` then `EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily()` (GameManager.cs:673–674).
- `EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily()` (EmployeeHelper.cs:91): `foreach (var e in GetEmployeeInstances(new EmployeeInstancesQueryInfo { excludeBeingReplaced = true })) e.WorkDaily();`
- `HRManager.WorkDaily()` override (Entities/HRManager.cs:30): `var plan = HrManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForHrManager(id); if (plan != null) { plan.TrainEmployees(); plan.PayHealthInsurance(); }`. Base `EmployeeInstance.WorkDaily()` is empty (EmployeeInstance.cs:754).
- `TrainEmployees()` has EXACTLY ONE caller: `HRManager.WorkDaily()`. It is NOT hooked to `GlobalEvents.onNewDay`, NOT a manager-specific tick, NOT `EmployeeHelper.RunDaily()` (that separate method handles aging/retirement/complaints/demand-generation).
- `TrainEmployees()` logic: for each assigned employee raise `characterData.skills[0].value` (primary) by `Mathf.RoundToInt(Mathf.Min(trainingTarget - value, 2f))` per day; each secondary skill by `Mathf.Min(trainingTarget - value, primaryDelta)` (≈1/day, clamped so it never overshoots and never exceeds the primary step). Every increment calls `employee.IncreaseWageFromTraining(delta)` (raises `hourlyWage` proportionally) and accumulates `EmployeeHelper.GetTrainingCost(employee, skillName, delta)`. Total × `TrainingPriceMultiplier` (`0.9f - 0.3f*HrManagerSkillValue/100f` → 0.9 at skill 0, 0.6 at skill 100) is charged: `GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe(-cost, new TransactionInfo("ba:transaction_hrtraining", {employee=name}), SaveGameManager.Current.Day - 1, null, force: true)` — tax-deductible ("ba:transaction_employeetraining_label"), forced, NO notification.
- `PayHealthInsurance()`: only if `HasActiveHealthInsurance()` (`healthInsurancePlan != null && HrManagerInstance != null && !HrManagerInstance.isBeingReplaced`). Cost = `max(NumberOfAssignedEmployees, HealthInsuranceHelper.MinimumEmployeesInCharge) * healthInsurancePlan.pricePerDayAndEmployee`, charged forced/tax-deductible to `headquartersAddress`, no notification.
- Constants: `HrManagerHelper.PrimarySkillTrainingPerDay = 2`, `HrManagerHelper.SecondarySkillTrainingPerDay = 1`.

DOES THE MANAGER NEED TO BE SCHEDULED?
- Not "always on", but the schedule gate is a PRECONDITION for assignment, not a per-day throttle:
  1. The assignment dropdown filters on `x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()` — you cannot attach an unscheduled manager to a plan.
  2. `ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans(BizManBusiness)` (ScheduleHelper.cs:388) runs on EVERY HQ schedule edit (`ScheduleDayButton` lines 168/237, `ScheduleHelper.UpdateEmployeesAfterWorkShiftChange` lines 191/221, `ScheduleAutoFillerHelper` line 76). For each plan of that HQ: `if (plan.HrManagerInstance != null && !plan.HrManagerInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()) plan.UnAssignEmployee();` — removing the manager's last HQ shift auto-detaches them from the plan.
- HOWEVER `EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily()` filters ONLY `excludeBeingReplaced = true` (EmployeeInstancesQueryInfo). It does NOT check attendance, roster hours, whether the HQ is "open" that day, or `isAbsent`. So once the manager is attached and still holds an HQ shift, `TrainEmployees()` fires every day at the flat 2/day rate regardless of how few hours/days they are rostered. Training is not proportional to hours worked. Absent-not-replaced employees are still processed; only `isBeingReplaced` skips.
- `EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()` (EmployeeInstance.cs:302): requires `IsAssignedToAnyBusiness()` (non-null `assignedAddress`) plus a `WorkShift.employeeId == id` in some `scheduleDays[].workShifts` of that building. Adding the shift runs `employee.UpdateWeeklyHoursAndDays(...)` and `employee.UpdateAssignedWorkStationItems()` — i.e. the manager needs a HQ workstation/desk item whose `suitableSkills`/`skillsRequired` includes `ba:skill_hrmanager` (WorkStationInfo.skillsRequired; SchedulePartitioner checks `workStation.skillsRequired.Contains(employee.GetPrimarySkill())`).
- The manager still draws salary daily via `EmployeeHelper.PayDailyWages()` → `PayWage()`, same as any employee. `replaceAbsentEmployees` (plan bool, default true) + Headhunter `HeadhunterPlan.assignedHrPlans` drive auto-replacement of an absent manager through `isBeingReplaced`.

UI ENTRY POINTS
- It is a SMARTPHONE APP, not a building panel: `AppName.BizMan` (the "BizMan" app). `BizMan.Open(Address newAddress = null, string tab = null)` (UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/BizMan.cs:60) → `FullMenu.ShowApp(AppName.BizMan)` → `business.SetAddress(addr)` → `business.SetInitialTab(tab)` → `business.Open()`. Deep-link pattern (from `PricingManagerPlan.OnClickShowPricingManager`): `fullMenu.bizMan.Open(headquartersAddress, "PricingManagers"); fullMenu.bizMan.business.pricingManagersPlanList.SelectPlanById(id);` — the HR analogue is `fullMenu.bizMan.business.hrManagersPlanList.SelectPlan(plan)` (used by the MyEmployees `EmployeeCellView` HR chip, EmployeeCellView.cs:123).
- `BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs()` (BizManBusiness.cs:222): when `buildingRegistration.businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters"` the tabs are `Schedule, PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters, Settings`. Tab id constant `BizMan.HrManagersTab = "HRManagers"` (BizMan.cs:25).
- The "HRManagers" tab container holds two serialized components, both fields on `BizManBusiness`:
  * `hrManagersPlanList` : `HrManagersPlanList` (BizManBusiness.cs:102) — MonoBehaviour rendering the left column: an entry per plan (manager name / "N/Max" info / health-insurance icon), a `ReorderableList`, and the "add plan" `buttonEntry`. Methods `AddPlan()`, `SelectPlan(HrManagerPlan)`, `RefreshManagersList()`, per-entry `ManagerDropdown`.
  * `hrHrManagerPlanUI` : `HrManagerPlanUI` (BizManBusiness.cs:100) — MonoBehaviour rendering the right-hand detail panel for the selected plan: `replaceAbsentEmployeesToggle` (→ `plan.replaceAbsentEmployees`), `trainingTargetSlider` + `trainingTargetValue` (→ `plan.trainingTarget` %, default 50), avg salary / avg satisfaction / avg primary-skill progress bars, `employeesScrollerController` (assigned list), `assignableEmployeesScrollerController` + `assignEmployeesList` (the assign UI), health-insurance info label + `cancelHealthInsuranceButton` + `upgradeHealthInsuranceButton` + `noHealthInsuranceInfoLabel`, and the `noManagerAssignedPopUp`.
- Classes under UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/ (folder) — note MonoBehaviours use namespace `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HRManagers` (capital HR), models use `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers`:
  * `HrManagersPlanList` (MonoBehaviour) — plan list / add / reorder / select / manager dropdown.
  * `HrManagerPlanUI` (MonoBehaviour) — the detail panel described above.
  * `EmployeesScrollerController : BaTable<EmployeeCellView, HrManagerEmployeeModel>` — the assigned/assignable employee tables (`Load(List<EmployeeInstance>, bool includeUnassignedEmployees, string managerId)`).
  * `EmployeeCellView : BaTableCellView<HrManagerEmployeeModel>` — one employee row: `assignToggle` → `hrHrManagerPlanUI.SetEmployeeAssigned(...)`, row click → jump to `fullMenu.myEmployees.DelayShowEmployee(...)`.
  * `HrManagerEmployeeModel : BaseEmployeeModel` — row data (name/wage/primary skill/satisfaction/insurance-demand text/`assigned` bool).
  * `HeadhunterEmployeeModel`, `HeadhunterEmployeesScrollerController` — the headhunter recruiting sub-view used from the HR plan.
- `NoManagerAssignedPopUp` (top-level class, NoManagerAssignedPopUp.cs) — dims the plan panel when no manager, offers an `employeeDropdown` and the plan `Delete` (`HudConfirm` "bizman_delete_plan_confirm").
- Prefab/window names are Unity asset-bundle assets referenced via `[SerializeField]` (`entryTemplate`, `buttonEntry`, `hrManagerPlanUI`, bronze/silver/gold health-insurance sprites) — not present in the decompiled C#. Tab objects are found at runtime under `BizManBusiness.containers.Find("HRManagers")` and `menu.Find("HRManagers")`.
- Tutorial hooks: `Tutorial/TutorialPointerHideConditionHasHrManagerPlan`, `...HasAssignedHrManagerToHrManagerPlan`, `...HasEmployeeAssignedToHrManagerPlan`, `Tutorial/HasEmployeeAssignedToHrManager`.

VISIBLE FEEDBACK THE VANILLA HR ROLE PRODUCES
- Indirect: rising skill/salary numbers in the panel bars, finance line items `TransactionInfo("ba:transaction_hrtraining")` and `("ba:transaction_healthinsurance", "ba:transactioncategory_healthinsuranceexpenses")`, and the daily summary. Training/insurance charges themselves are silent (`showNotification: false`, forced).
- `AI.Employees.LowSkillComplaint`: an assigned employee under skill 75 AND under `plan.trainingTarget` sends phone message `ba:messagetype_employee_contact_complaint_low_skill`; it auto-resolves once trained past target (LowSkillComplaint.cs:29 reads `HrManagerHelper.GetPlanFromId(employeeInstance.assignedHrManagerPlanId).trainingTarget`). This is the main "the manager is doing its job" signal.
- The richer feedback template is `LogisticsManagerPlan` (relevant to our mod's delivery goal): a dedicated `Contact` ("logistics_alerts", `Contact.EnsurePermanentContact(..., ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods, ...)`), `SendDeliveryReport(...)` sending `TextMessage`s ("ba:messagetype_phone_logistics_manager_delivery_no_stock" / "…no_available_space"), and `NotifyDeliveryAlerts()` aggregating into `Notifications.Show(NotificationType.Warning, "delivery_alert_notification[_multiple]", …, onClick => open the contact)`. `PricingManagerPlan.NotifyMispricedItems()` shows the notification+deep-link pattern: `Notifications.Show(NotificationType.Info, "notifications_PricingManager_mispriced_items", {employeeName, amount}, 4f, null, OnClickShowPricingManager)` where the click opens the BizMan tab and selects the plan by id.

HEALTH-INSURANCE SUB-FEATURE = MODEL OF AN OPTIONAL PER-PLAN SETTING (analogous to our per-store limits)
- The setting itself is just a nullable reference field on the plan: `HrManagerPlan.healthInsurancePlan` : `HealthInsurancePlan` (fields: `planType` — enum `HealthInsurancePlanType` Bronze/Silver/Gold; `pricePerDayAndEmployee` : float). Persisted with the plan; null = feature off.
- It is NOT configured in the BizMan panel. It is negotiated through an NPC:
  * Gate: `HrManagerPlan.CanHaveHealthInsurancePlan` => `healthInsurancePlan == null && HrManagerInstance != null && !healthInsurancePlanOffers.Exists(o => o.hrManagerPlanId == id && !o.negotiationFinished)`.
  * `Dialogs.HealthInsuranceManagerDialog` (hospital contact "hospital_health_insurance_manager", `GameManager.hospitalAddress`) → `StartPartnership` → input component `UI.Dialog.HealthInsurancePartnershipSettings` (dropdown of `hrManagerPlans.Where(x => x.CanHaveHealthInsurancePlan)` + plan-type dropdown gated by `HrManagerSkillValue >= planType.GetMinSkillForPlan()`).
  * Confirm → `new HealthInsurancePlanOffer(plan.id, planType)` added to `SaveGameManager.Current.healthInsurancePlanOffers`; `GameEvent.Invoke("ba:gameevent_newhealthinsuranceplanoffer")`; player + NPC `TextMessage`s.
  * `HealthInsurancePlanOffer : NegotiationOffer` (`deadlineDay = Day + 1`, `initialOfferPrice`, `minOfferPrice`). `SendOffer()` messages a counter-offer via a `TextMessage.ContextAction { type = HealthInsurancePlanOffer, healthPlanOfferId = id }`; price derived from `HrManagerSkillValue`, `HealthInsuranceHelper.GetEmployeesInChargePower(NumberOfAssignedEmployees)`, `HealthInsuranceHelper.GetExperiencePower((HrManagerInstance as HRManager)?.experienceWithInsurancesInYears)`, and player `ba:skill_negotiation`.
  * `AcceptOffer(pricePerDayAndEmployee)` → `HrManagerPlan.healthInsurancePlan = new HealthInsurancePlan { planType, pricePerDayAndEmployee }`; `GameEvent.Invoke("ba:gameevent_healthinsuranceplanaccepted")`.
- In the panel `HrManagerPlanUI.SetUpHealthInsuranceInfo()` only DISPLAYS status and offers: `CancelInsurance()` → `plan.CancelHealthInsurancePlan()` (just nulls the field, after `HudConfirm`); `UpgradeInsurance()` → `plan.UpgradeHealthInsurancePlan()` (`GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe` for the tier delta, `showNotification: true`, then `planType = planType.Next()`), enabled only when `CanUpgradeHealthInsurancePlan()` (not Gold, skill >= next tier's `GetMinSkillForPlan()`).
- Daily cost billed from `PayHealthInsurance()` inside `HRManager.WorkDaily()` (see above).
- It also feeds employee job-demands: `Entities.Employee.JobDemands.Requirements.HasHealthInsurance` checks the assigned employee's plan's `healthInsurancePlan`; `HRManager` itself is exempt from health-insurance demands (`EmployeeInstance.AddRandomDemand`: `this is HRManager` → skip `JobDemandHelper.HealthInsuranceDemands`).
- Design takeaway for our mod: an optional per-store setting is nothing more than a nullable/collection field on the plan object persisted with it. The negotiation/NPC ceremony is separable scaffolding; our "per-store limits" can be a plain `List<StoreLimit>` field set directly in our config UI/console.

CROSS-REFERENCES OF INTEREST
- `Buildings.BuildingTypes.Special.MovingCompany.BizManTransfer` moves `hrManagerPlan.headquartersAddress` when a HQ business relocates.
- `Helpers.BusinessHelper` (line ~999) clears HR plans for a HQ when the business is closed/sold.
- `HeadhuntersAutomaticReplacementTab` / `HeadhunterPlan.assignedHrPlans` (string[2]) — a Headhunter plan can be told to auto-replace the manager of up to 2 HR plans.

keyTypes.name: Buildings.Office.Headquarters.LogisticsManagerPlan
keyTypes.note: Sibling role and the better template for the mod: assignedEmployeeId + headquartersAddress + targetAddress(warehouse) + List<LogisticsManagerPlanDestination> destinations; MaxDestinations from ba:skill_logisticsmanager; dedicated Contact 'logistics_alerts' + SendDeliveryReport TextMessages + NotifyDeliveryAlerts Notifications.Show. modFeasibility:
Native (no Harmony): reuse a REAL skill for the store manager — there is no ba:skill_storemanager, so use ba:skill_logisticsmanager (closest: already restocks stores) or ba:skill_hrmanager. A candidate with that skill is produced by the normal recruitment campaign / headhunter, hires via EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate, shows in My Employees (target 3), and is scheduled with the vanilla schedule UI (target 4) with zero patching. The mod keeps its own plan list in its JSON file keyed by EmployeeInstance.id, mirroring HrManagerPlan (assignedEmployeeId, headquartersAddress, supervisedStoreAddresses, per-store limits). Drive it from GlobalEvents.onNewDay, gating on the same conditions the game uses (!isBeingReplaced; IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() to require an HQ shift; optionally IsEmployeeAvailable()). Multi-store supervision + per-store limits are pure mod data (targets 5-6). Stocking via delivery = manage each supervised BuildingRegistration's DeliveryContract (target 7) with the confirmed DeliveryHelper API. Visible feedback (target 1) is fully native: Notifications.Show, a dedicated Contact ('store_manager') sending TextMessages, and TransactionInfo line items — copy the LogisticsManagerPlan pattern.

Needs Harmony (bundle it flat in Dependencies/, as another local mod already does): (a) the ONE requirement that cannot be done natively is target 2 — a real BizMan 'Store Managers' tab injected next to HRManagers/LogisticsManagers; BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs and the tab prefabs are game assets. Without Harmony, the mod's limits/assignment UI stays in ModOptions + console commands (today's shape) or a bespoke overlay. (b) For exact lifecycle parity, postfix EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily (or HRManager.WorkDaily), ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans (auto-detach on unschedule), and EmployeeInstance.OnRemove (cleanup). (c) A custom EmployeeInstance subclass is NOT safe — the Odin/Newtonsoft save is keyed on concrete types compiled into the game; a mod subclass would not round-trip and could corrupt vanilla saves. Keep the manager a stock EmployeeInstance and hold all extra state in mod-side data.

Infeasible / not worth it: faithfully re-adding HrManagerPlan-style persistence into GameInstance from a mod (no save hook, and injecting fields into the game's serialized graph is fragile). Store manager state must live in the mod's own file.
